methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort study with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, NUC-naïve chronic HBV patients (n=195) with adequate follow-up (median 7.4 years, range 1.0-17.9 years). HCC surveillance standardized (ultrasound or CT/MRI every 3-6 months) with diagnostic criteria specified (percutaneous biopsy or imaging with arterial hyperenhancement + washout). Baseline characteristics comprehensively documented. Main limitations: single center, no external validation, variable follow-up duration, relatively small HCC event number (n=19, ~10% event rate) which may compromise multivariate model stability. No discussion of proportional hazards assumption testing.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Directly addresses critical clinical problem: HCC develops in some patients despite nucleos(t)ide analogue antiviral therapy for chronic HBV, requiring better risk stratification to guide surveillance intensity and preventive strategies. Proposes non-invasive biomarker (12-HHT from routine blood sample) enabling striking risk stratification: 63% versus 1% HCC incidence at 10 years when combined with FIB-4 index. Offers practical clinical utility for personalizing patient monitoring if prospectively validated.

reporting_quality.justification: Adequate STROBE adherence: clear study objectives, patient inclusion/exclusion criteria, institutional ethics approval documented, baseline characteristics thoroughly presented in Table 1, statistical methods detailed, results with hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction appropriately applied for multiple metabolite comparisons (identifying only 12-HHT as significant after correction). Limitations: FDR correction not applied to clinical variable comparisons, pre-registration not mentioned, no data availability statement. Mechanistic discussion of 12-HHT-BLT2-intestinal barrier is speculative.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors state this is first study evaluating PUFA metabolites for HCC prediction during NUC therapy in chronic HBV. However, lipidomic analyses for HCC biomarker identification previously conducted (references 19-20 demonstrating altered PUFA metabolites in HBV-related HCC). Novel population-specific contribution (NUC-treated patients) and functional metric combination (12-HHT + FIB-4), but mechanism remains speculative. Represents incremental advance in biomarker field.

writing_presentation.justification: Introduction effectively motivated with clear clinical gap identification. Methods adequately described with laboratory assay details and statistical approach. Results logically presented with ROC curves, Kaplan-Meier curves showing dramatic risk stratification, and hazard ratios with confidence intervals. However: Discussion mechanism (12-HHT binding BLT2 receptor enhancing intestinal barrier function preventing HCC) is largely speculative, explicitly acknowledged by authors ("Further studies are required to elucidate the mechanisms"). Dense results section with multiple supplementary figures required. Overall readable but could benefit from mechanism section expansion with caveats.

key_strengths: First study evaluating association between PUFA metabolites and HCC development during NUC therapy in chronic HBV patients using targeted lipidomic analysis

Striking clinical risk stratification: 12-HHT combined with FIB-4 achieves 63% 10-year HCC incidence for high FIB-4/low 12-HHT versus 1% for low FIB-4/high 12-HHT, providing practical biomarker utility

Appropriate statistical methodology including Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction for multiple metabolite comparisons identifying only 12-HHT as robust predictor; long median follow-up with standardized surveillance protocol
key_concerns: Small number of HCC events (n=19) relative to cohort size (N=195) limits multivariate Cox model stability and generalizability of hazard ratio estimates
Single-center retrospective design with no external validation; all patients from Japan limits generalizability across geographic regions and healthcare systems
Proposed biological mechanism (12-HHT→BLT2→intestinal barrier enhancement) entirely speculative with no functional validation; study demonstrates association not causation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid retrospective cohort study identifying 12-HHT as strong predictor of HCC during antiviral therapy with compelling clinical stratification in combination with FIB-4. However, single-center design with small event number and entirely speculative mechanism limit impact. Tier 3 appropriate for promising biomarker research requiring external prospective validation before clinical implementation.
